The participle is the nomen rectum of תּוֹרַת, so the relational for the ASV writes for that construct relation is its own (rule 19); the unit is discontinuous around the article's her that (rule 25) and heads on the lexeme-bearing beareth (rule 24).

The ASV writes no word for this preposition's own relation: whether is the opening member of the correlative pair the disjunction אוֹ is rendered by, not a rendering of לְ. Rule 14's exception hands an opening correlative to another morpheme only where that morpheme is itself what the correlative says — a present negative for neither, the מִן of a range for both — and a preposition meaning for is not what whether says; standing in the slot where a for would have stood is position, not sense. So the preposition is unrepresented (rule 40), exactly as the second לְ of the pair is. The competing reading, taken by the earlier alignment, gives whether to this לְ on positional grounds; a third reading leaves whether added under rule 30 (rule 8).

review_notes: Correction: whether (t032) is moved from the first לְ (s021) to אוֹ (s024), which now holds the discontinuous correlative pair whether ... or headed on or, and s021 joins s025 as unrepresented. Rule 14 lets a morpheme other than the connective take an opening correlative only where that morpheme is itself what the correlative says; a preposition meaning for is not what whether says, so the pair stays with the disjunction that is written. Every other unit is retained as accepted.
